title: Dock Walk
brief: You walk the Meridian Logistics distribution centre at shift change, from receiving docks to dispatch, as an internal auditor. The site manager wants a view of the whole flow before a major retail customer's audit. Warehouse safety is managed separately and is outside this visit. You have 12 visit points.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: What to do when a count is wrong
Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Inbound pallet IN-5521 of customer goods has crushed cartons; it is put away in bay 14 with no damage record and no customer notice.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer goods are customer property; damage must be recorded and reported.
evidence.missedExplanation: Watch what happens to damaged goods.

evidence.text: Cold store temperature logger TL-4 verification is overdue by 6 weeks.
evidence.whyItMatters: Monitoring devices must be verified at the planned interval.

evidence.text: Pick instruction at zone C is issue 5; the system shows issue 6 with a new slotting map for 40 locations.
evidence.whyItMatters: Current instructions must be at the point of use.

evidence.text: Scanner SC-12 at zone C fails to read 1 in 10 labels; pickers key codes by hand.
evidence.whyItMatters: Manual keying increases errors; repair would reduce risk.

evidence.text: Customer returnable crates (about 60, owner code RC-7) are stacked outside, unlabeled and mixed with company crates.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer property must be identified and protected.

evidence.text: Load check records for this morning's 12 loads are complete and signed.
2 pallets in outbound lane 3 carry labels for order OR-9902, but the system shows them as order OR-9920.
Shift lead: "A wrong count goes on hold in the red lane until checked and authorized."
Receiving discrepancy log is complete for the week.
Temperature records for the week are complete and within range.
Floor markings are faded in one aisle; the safety team has a work order.
evidence.whyItMatters: Safety matter outside this visit and already in hand.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Outside this visit and already addressed.

decisions.prompt: What needs action before the next dispatch wave?
options: Hold the 2 mislabeled pallets in lane 3 and correct them, and segregate and report the damaged customer pallet
Stop all dispatch for the day
decisions.rationale: Issues that could send the wrong goods or hide damage come first.

containment: Hold lane 3 pallets until labels match the system; segregate pallet IN-5521
correction: Relabel, report damage to the customer, label the crates, verify TL-4, and post issue 6
cause: No receiving damage step, no logger due alert, and no issue control at pick faces
corrective: Add a damage step at receiving, logger due alerts, and a weekly instruction issue check
effectiveness: Repeat the walk monthly for three months

debriefText.falseFinding: A handwritten rota and a known safety work order are not quality findings.
